stories.body: The United States has launched “Operation Economic Outcast,” an expanded secondary-sanctions campaign targeting Iran’s oil revenue and its digital-assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said countries and companies must choose between doing business with the US and Iran, warning that participants in transactions converting Iranian oil into revenue could be targeted and cut off from the dollar system. The campaign follows months of war and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz; Iran has vowed to retaliate, while questions remain over how forcefully Washington will act against China, Iran’s largest oil customer.
stories.headline: US launches sweeping sanctions campaign aimed at cutting off Iran's economic lifelines

stories.body: An oil tanker was damaged after being struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz off Oman, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency. No casualties were reported. The incident comes as Iran maintains an effective blockade of the strategic waterway following US and Israeli strikes in late February, with attacks on ships and severe disruption to shipping continuing to endanger seafarers and port workers.
stories.headline: Oil tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz off Oman

stories.body: President Donald Trump said US tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts and steel will rise to 50% from January 1, 2027, escalating a trade dispute after negotiations with Ottawa collapsed. Trump said the US did not need Canada and urged companies to build in the United States, while Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said his government would not accept a deal at any price and was prepared to respond to what it considers unjustified tariffs. The announcement has intensified concerns over the effects on tightly integrated North American manufacturing and supply chains.
stories.headline: Trump threatens 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles, parts and steel after trade talks collapse

stories.body: The United States has removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, ending a designation in place since 1979 and clearing a major obstacle to foreign investment and the country’s reintegration into the global economy. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the move recognized commitments by President Ahmed al-Sharaa’s government to distance itself from international terrorism. The decision also removes the former al-Nusra Front, now Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, from a related terrorism designation, as Washington seeks to support Syria’s recovery and draw it away from Iranian and Russian influence.
stories.headline: US removes Syria from list of state sponsors of terrorism

stories.body: At least 30 people have been killed after heavy rain caused a massive waste mound at the Dar es Salam landfill outside Guinea’s capital, Conakry, to collapse onto nearby homes and makeshift dwellings. Six people were seriously injured, while rescue teams used excavators and other equipment to search the debris for survivors. The landfill had been scheduled for closure because of the danger it posed during the rainy season, but families remained in the area when the collapse occurred.
stories.headline: Guinea landfill collapse kills at least 30 people as search for survivors continues

stories.body: The Trump administration is preparing to revoke business and tourist visas held by as many as 200,000 people who have applied for or are seeking asylum in the United States, according to State Department documents and officials cited by the Associated Press. The proposed action would cover B1 and B2 visas issued from 2016 to 2026 and could become the largest single mass visa revocation in US history. Officials said the change would not automatically result in deportation, as many people with pending asylum cases would be moved into another immigration category while their cases continue.
stories.headline: Trump administration plans to revoke visas held by up to 200,000 asylum seekers

stories.body: Tens of thousands of people remain displaced as the human-caused Hawk Fire burns near Reno, Nevada, where it has destroyed more than 30 homes and spread close to densely populated neighbourhoods. About 24,000 people were still under evacuation orders on Monday, down from more than 40,000 at the height of the emergency, while many more remained on alert. Fire crews have begun to gain some containment, but shifting winds, heavy smoke and the risk of renewed spread have kept schools closed and emergency services on high alert.
stories.headline: Nevada wildfire threatens Reno as tens of thousands remain under evacuation orders

stories.body: The Trump administration is considering a proposal to charge employers more than $100,000 for skilled-worker visas, a move that would sharply raise the cost of bringing foreign professionals to the United States. The selected briefing did not include hydrated source material for this story.
stories.headline: Trump officials propose charging more than $100,000 for skilled-worker visas

stories.body: Spain’s government is creating a unified command to manage the migration and security crisis in Ceuta, nearly a month after tens of thousands of people crossed into the autonomous city from Morocco. The National Security Council is expected to declare a situation of national-security interest and appoint Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres to coordinate the response with local authorities, intelligence services and relevant ministries. The measure is intended to address the humanitarian, housing, health and public-order pressures created by the sustained arrivals.
stories.headline: Spain creates unified command for Ceuta nearly a month after mass migrant crossing

stories.body: Spain’s Health Ministry and regional governments will send 45,000 vaccine doses to Ceuta to bolster prevention efforts amid the prolonged migrant crisis: 15,000 measles, mumps and rubella doses and 10,000 each for diphtheria-tetanus, chickenpox and polio. Authorities say the measure is designed to protect both migrants and unvaccinated residents without disrupting routine vaccination programmes. Health officials stress that there is no epidemic, but medical services have faced intense pressure as thousands of migrants have lived in precarious conditions since the mass arrivals began at the end of July.
stories.headline: Spain sends 45,000 vaccine doses to Ceuta as migrant crisis strains health services

stories.body: Spanish police have seized 1,410 kilograms of cocaine and arrested three men in A Pobra do Caramiñal, Galicia, in an operation targeting the long-established Os Fanchos smuggling clan. Investigators say the drugs were landed by sea near O Conchido beach and hidden in nearby buildings before they could be transferred to a cell linked to the Balkan cartel. The operation, supported by the US Drug Enforcement Administration, led to the detention of the alleged clan leader, an associate and a Croatian national who police believe was overseeing delivery for the intended recipients.
stories.headline: Police seize 1,410 kilograms of cocaine and arrest members of Galician smuggling clan

stories.body: Intense thunderstorms bringing torrential rain, hail and strong winds caused flooding, fallen trees and transport disruption across Tarragona province before moving toward the Penedès and Barcelona metropolitan area. Rainfall totals included nearly 89 millimetres in three hours at Vinyols i els Arcs, while wind gusts reached 117 kilometres per hour in parts of Catalonia. Rail services on several Rodalies lines were suspended or disrupted, emergency services received hundreds of calls, and authorities urged residents not to travel through flooded areas or approach rivers and ravines.
stories.headline: Severe storms and hail cause flooding and transport disruption in Tarragona

stories.body: The global average sea-surface temperature outside polar regions reached a record 21.1C on August 22, according to the EU’s Copernicus Climate Change Service, narrowly surpassing the previous high set in March 2024. Scientists say the timing is particularly striking because global ocean temperatures usually peak in March or April, and El Niño is expected to strengthen further toward the end of the year. Copernicus links the record to decades of human-driven warming compounded by El Niño, warning that warmer oceans can intensify extreme weather, raise sea levels and damage marine ecosystems.
stories.headline: Global sea-surface temperature reaches a new record of 21.1C

stories.body: USTEC, Catalonia’s largest public-school teachers’ union, says a strike planned for September 8, the first day of the school year, is now difficult to avoid because the Education Department has not resumed negotiations during the summer. The union is demanding a timetable for structural reforms, including smaller class sizes, stronger inclusive education, more resources for newcomer classrooms, protection for Catalan and measures to address extreme heat in schools. It warned that the one-day strike could be the start of a wider labour dispute during the first term unless the regional government engages in meaningful talks.
stories.headline: Catalan teachers maintain strike planned for first day of school year

stories.body: Barcelona’s Guàrdia Urbana has arrested a suspect accused of setting 18 fires that burned 127 rubbish containers in the Sant Gervasi and Pedralbes neighbourhoods between May and August. The fires also damaged 11 vehicles, protected paving in Plaça del Monestir, a school wall and a gas pipe at Escola Abat Oliba Loreto, forcing the school to go without gas service for two days. The city estimates the damage at about €115,000.
stories.headline: Barcelona arrests suspect accused of setting fire to 127 rubbish containers

stories.body: Bellvitge Hospital treated eight patients with severe heart failure in a single week in mid-August, performing four heart transplants and implanting ventricular-assist devices in four others. Two of the devices were long-term implants, while the other two were intended as temporary support pending possible transplants. The hospital said more than 30 medical and nursing professionals across cardiac surgery, cardiology, anaesthesiology, intensive care and transplant coordination worked together to complete the procedures successfully.
stories.headline: Bellvitge Hospital performs four heart transplants and four ventricular-assist implants in one week
